theme: Hosea and Gomer; the broken marriage as Israel’s story
readingInstruction: Read Hosea 1:1-3:5. Hosea is told to marry a woman who will be unfaithful, and his marriage becomes a picture of God and Israel. This is one of the most moving stories in the Bible. Read the whole of chapter 2, and ask what God is feeling.
settingTheScene: Hosea prophesied in the northern kingdom in the decades before its fall, from the time of Jeroboam II to about 722 BC. He was a contemporary of Amos, but the tone of his message is different. Amos spoke of justice, and Hosea speaks of love. His own marriage becomes a living sermon. God tells him to marry a woman who will be unfaithful, so that he can feel something of what God feels over Israel’s unfaithfulness.
observation: “Go, take to yourself a wife of whoredom and have children of whoredom, for the land commits great whoredom by forsaking the LORD” (1:2).
The children are named Jezreel, No Mercy (Lo-ruhamah), and Not My People (Lo-ammi) (1:4-9).

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea… In the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, it shall be said to them, Children of the living God” (1:10).
“She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the wine, and the oil” (2:8).
“Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her” (2:14).
“And I will betroth you to me forever. I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love and in mercy” (2:19).
“And I will say to Not My People, You are my people; and he shall say, You are my God” (2:23).
“Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, even as the LORD loves the children of Israel” (3:1).
interpretation:
The story of Hosea is shocking on purpose. God tells his prophet to marry Gomer, and the text implies that she will be unfaithful. Their children are given names that preach: Jezreel, a reminder of Jehu’s bloodshed; No Mercy; and Not My People. The names are a message of judgment. A nation that broke covenant will lose the privileges of the covenant.

Chapter 2 is a courtroom drama that turns into a love song. First, God speaks as a wronged husband. Israel has run after her lovers, the Baals, thinking they were the ones who gave her grain, wine, and oil. “She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain.” Idolatry is ingratitude. It credits the gifts to the wrong giver. God says he will strip away what she was relying on, so that she will see.

Then, in verse 14, the tone changes completely. “Therefore, behold, I will allure her.” After the judgment, God does not abandon her. He takes her to the wilderness, the place of their first love, and “speaks tenderly to her.” The word means to speak to the heart. And he promises to make the Valley of Achor, the valley of trouble, “a door of hope.” He promises a new marriage: “I will betroth you to me forever.” The phrase is repeated three times. And it comes with a list of the gifts of the new covenant: righteousness, justice, steadfast love, mercy, and faithfulness. The result: “You shall know the LORD.”

The names are reversed. “I will say to Not My People, You are my people.” Mercy is given to those who had no mercy.

Chapter 3 is the costly part of the story. Hosea is told to buy back his wife from slavery or prostitution, for fifteen shekels of silver and some barley. This is the picture of redemption. God loves the unlovable and pays the price to bring her home. And the chapter ends by looking forward to the day when Israel will seek the LORD and “David their king.”
connection: Paul quotes Hosea 1:10 and 2:23 in Romans 9:25-26 and Peter quotes them in 1 Peter 2:10 to describe the church: “Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.” Hosea’s redemption of Gomer is a picture of Christ’s redeeming his bride (Ephesians 5:25-27; 1 Corinthians 6:20). Jesus said, “I came not to call the righteous, but sinners” (Mark 2:17).
application:
Reflect on being “Not My People” and now “My People.” What does mercy mean to you?

Ask God to speak tenderly to you in your wilderness.

Think about whom you are tempted to give up on. How does Hosea’s love challenge you?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for loving you when you were not his people.
Thank him for buying you back.
Ask him to allure you and speak tenderly to you.
